cards.heading: Vitis communis, agrestis and nigra
cards.notes: Clustered units on peduncles; pointed palmate blades and curling tendrils; two separate cuttings cross but there is no third shared upright axis or common base.
cards.plate: BL Sloane MS 4016 f101r (three illustrated cuttings)

cards.heading: Voynich f35v
cards.notes: Comparison target; two lateral round-lobed blades at different heights; root spread measured about 2.5 times farther to the left than to the right of the main stem.

cards.heading: Vitis
cards.notes: Continuous sinuous woody axis and tendrils spanning two pages; no separate rounded units securely visible; lower drawing ends in a cut or tapered axis.
cards.plate: BnF Latin 6823 ff164v–165r (sinuous axis through gutter)

cards.heading: Edera nigra
cards.notes: Small clustered units, triangular to angular leaves; the lower axis reaches the page edge, excluding a root assessment.

cards.heading: Galla
cards.notes: Occupied cups and separate round spots in a compact rounded-leaf upper crown; no securely isolated below-crown side pair; lower lines near the base are faint and may include neighboring plant marks.

cards.heading: Brionia / Vitis alba
cards.notes: Open radial groups of small rounds, broad angular blades, two long divergent tapering portions of a single large root body.

cards.heading: Ebulus
cards.notes: Small outlined units in hemispherical heads on a tall pinnate pattern; roots extend to page edges and their terminal topology and ratio are uncertain.
cards.plate: BnF Latin 6823 f63v (large plant at left)

cards.heading: Uva minoris
cards.notes: Compact drooping bunches, pointed leaves on a curved axis, and no common roots in the depicted cutting.

cards.heading: Glandes
cards.notes: Cupped fruits and visibly rounded lobes on a short twig; no two isolated lower blades below a crown and no root.

cards.heading: Galla
cards.notes: Separated lower lobed blades feed a near-compact canopy with curled upper edges; cups flank free oval spots; basal roots spread mainly downward with no three hooked tips visible.

cards.heading: Ebulus
cards.notes: Open small rounded units arranged at radial stalk ends; repeating pinnate stem tiers; crossing branches belong to its root system, not aerial side stems.

cards.heading: Brionia
cards.notes: Scattered uncapped round units at leaf bases, no two clusters; long bifurcating root without asymmetric horizontal spread.

cards.heading: Edera nigra
cards.notes: Uncapped small clusters and angled to cordate leaves; a faint basal junction is visible on the full scan; a single winding support/axis does not meet the specified doubled crossing.

evidence.mask_spec: Coordinates are XYXY in pixels at reference dimensions. Cover rectangles in warm grey RGB (228,225,215), leaving the rest unchanged. Crop rectangles, juxtapose adjacent halves where applicable, then keep within 800 x 720 pixels. Seed 3506823 sets the order for the recorded preparation. At decision points where the crop concealed a contour, compare the full scan after the masked pass.
evidence.method: One observer fixed the checklist after seeing Yale f35v and the published BnF ivy comparator but before opening the other images. The same observer located and masked headings and then scored shuffled codes. Familiar shapes and preparation exposed specimen identities in some cases. The experiment is caption-masked with incomplete observer blinding. Residual prose beside contours can remain. Counts record depiction only. Separate cuttings and their crossings were never pooled into a single plant. The BnF vine occupies a two-page card with the center gutter. The abbreviated Sloane grape plate adds a second depiction from the same witness. The f60v eleborum illustration, Egerton f46r Herba vitis illustration of a distinct herb, and Sloane f102v plate without the designated Bryonia heading were not treated as substitutes for the named entries.
evidence.rubric:
# Public f35v motif comparison, fixed before opening the additional plates

Previously seen: Beinecke f35v, the black-ivy detail and Ethel Voynich oak-grape note reproduced on p. 24 of Zandbergen's 2012 slides, and full BnF latin 6823 f60r. Expected familiarity with ordinary silhouettes of the named plants. New comparator categories fixed using headings and documented plant names only. Use two compact Tractatus de herbis witnesses as available, Latin 6823 and Egerton 747, preferentially both witnesses per group. Seek the named black ivy and oak/gall tree, with three depicted alternatives (grape, elder and a lobed-leaf rooted herb, white bryony where catalogued). Where the requested entry has multiple drawings, retain all candidates or use separately illustrated entries if the source distinguishes them before viewing, rather than pick a nearest shape. Keep captions and neighboring plants outside the illustration where possible. When contours touch words, neutral mask the text without removing contours and log the exception. Record plates under shuffled codes before joining the identities. This is caption-masked, with one observer and incomplete blinding.

Use only outlines of the drawing: color may locate a contour, but it earns no points. For each feature use 1 visible, 0 visibly discordant or visibly missing on a complete plate, ? genuinely ambiguous or cropped. Record all 12 codes and matched count per region, with possible upper counts for unknowns. Equal weights; no hypothesis test. Describe where matches arise. Multiple manuscripts can transmit a drawing tradition, so report each witness without treating them as independent statistical draws.

Fruit (F)
F1. At least two discrete clusters of three or more rounded enclosed units, counting each unit once; scattered solitary fruits do not count.
F2. At least one such cluster terminates a distinct stalk, with recognizable grouping and no enclosing common fruit body or backing leaf.
F3. No acorn-like cup, enclosing husk, or lobed capsule around the rounded units; mark unknown if outlines are unreadable, zero if no rounded units.

Leaf (L)
L1. At least two individually outlined side leaves attach at distinct levels below the top foliage.
L2. Those side leaves are simple and visibly lobed, with at least two broad rounded lobes per side.
L3. The strongest lobing repeats along the long axis on both sides of the leaf; do not count a three- to five-point palmate leaf, a smooth small leaf, or individual leaflets along a rachis.

Crown/stems (C)
C1. A compact upper foliage outline distinguishable from lower lateral leaves or fruit.
C2. Multiple upward stalks fan toward that upper outline from a relatively narrow common point or band.
C3. Two lower lateral stems visibly cross in front of or around a distinct upright axis; a single fork without crossing does not count.

Roots (R)
R1. Clearly drawn roots and aerial stems meet at a common basal junction.
R2. Major lateral roots or primary branches bear at least three recognizable hooked or curved tips in aggregate.
R3. Strongly asymmetric lateral spread, roughly 2:1 or greater from the stem center measured against opposite side, with the longest root roughly horizontal for much of its run.

For a caption-free target, all 12 features are the prespecified matches; F2 and C3 will also be reported under a sensitivity analysis dropping either if attachment or topology proves uncertain on the scan. The rubric is target-conditioned, so results test specificity among documented controls, not identification in the abstract.
evidence.scoring_key: Per card and region, 1 is visible correspondence, 0 is absent or discordant, ? is obscured or ambiguous. Range counts definite to possible matches.
evidence.sensitivity: Dropping F2 changes fruit-perfect controls from 7 of 12 with 3/3 to the same 7 with 2/2. Dropping C3 preserves all control ranks because C3 is zero for every control. Dropping either criterion leaves the region split unchanged. Ignoring the side-leaf position requirement would raise the foliage match for Latin 6823 galla and glandes because the rounded lobes are visible elsewhere in their drawings.

detail.statement: An outline checklist applied to 12 caption-masked illustrations from three manuscripts in the Tractatus de herbis tradition gives full fruit scores to both black-ivy plates, both elder plates, one bryony plate and both Sloane grape views. The Egerton galla tree best reproduces the combination of offset rounded-lobed side leaves and compact crown. BnF galla and glandes also carry rounded lobing, with cupped fruits on all three oak plates. No comparator visibly meets the doubled aerial crossing or hooked, strongly asymmetric root criteria, and all match at most seven of the 12 features even if uncertain features count as matches. The black-ivy fruit parallel and oak foliage parallel are regional correspondences, with insufficient specificity for a botanical anchor.
detail.title: Replicate the f35v motif scores with independent masked annotators

statement: An outline checklist applied to 12 caption-masked illustrations from three manuscripts in the Tractatus de herbis tradition gives full fruit scores to both black-ivy plates, both elder plates, one bryony plate and both Sloane grape views. The Egerton galla tree best reproduces the combination of offset rounded-lobed side leaves and compact crown. BnF galla and glandes also carry rounded lobing, with cupped fruits on all three oak plates. No comparator visibly meets the doubled aerial crossing or hooked, strongly asymmetric root criteria, and all match at most seven of the 12 features even if uncertain features count as matches. The black-ivy fruit parallel and oak foliage parallel are regional correspondences, with insufficient specificity for a botanical anchor.

experiment.json.summary: Score f35v against caption-masked black-ivy, oak, grape, elder and bryony illustrations by region.

step.json.check: Give the frozen outline rubric and randomly coded crops to two observers who have not seen the proposed identifications, with headings masked by a separate preparer. Compare calls region by region before revealing the panel identities. Confirm whether two oak leaves genuinely sit below the crown, adjudicate the clipped roots, and report exact agreement and sensitivity to omitting F2 and C3. Treat the three manuscripts as related witnesses and use no Voynich label or proposed text.

cards.heading: Vitis communis, agrestis and nigra
cards.notes: Clustered units on peduncles; pointed palmate blades and curling tendrils; two separate cuttings cross but there is no third shared upright axis or common base.
cards.plate: BL Sloane MS 4016 f101r (three illustrated cuttings)

cards.heading: Voynich f35v
cards.notes: Comparison target; two lateral round-lobed blades at different heights; root spread measured about 2.5 times farther to the left than to the right of the main stem.

cards.heading: Vitis
cards.notes: Continuous sinuous woody axis and tendrils spanning two pages; no separate rounded units securely visible; lower drawing ends in a cut or tapered axis.
cards.plate: BnF Latin 6823 ff164v–165r (sinuous axis through gutter)

cards.heading: Edera nigra
cards.notes: Small clustered units, triangular to angular leaves; the lower axis reaches the page edge, excluding a root assessment.

cards.heading: Galla
cards.notes: Occupied cups and separate round spots in a compact rounded-leaf upper crown; no securely isolated below-crown side pair; lower lines near the base are faint and may include neighboring plant marks.

cards.heading: Brionia / Vitis alba
cards.notes: Open radial groups of small rounds, broad angular blades, two long divergent tapering portions of a single large root body.

cards.heading: Ebulus
cards.notes: Small outlined units in hemispherical heads on a tall pinnate pattern; roots extend to page edges and their terminal topology and ratio are uncertain.
cards.plate: BnF Latin 6823 f63v (large plant at left)

cards.heading: Uva minoris
cards.notes: Compact drooping bunches, pointed leaves on a curved axis, and no common roots in the depicted cutting.

cards.heading: Glandes
cards.notes: Cupped fruits and visibly rounded lobes on a short twig; no two isolated lower blades below a crown and no root.

cards.heading: Galla
cards.notes: Separated lower lobed blades feed a near-compact canopy with curled upper edges; cups flank free oval spots; basal roots spread mainly downward with no three hooked tips visible.

cards.heading: Ebulus
cards.notes: Open small rounded units arranged at radial stalk ends; repeating pinnate stem tiers; crossing branches belong to its root system, not aerial side stems.

cards.heading: Brionia
cards.notes: Scattered uncapped round units at leaf bases, no two clusters; long bifurcating root without asymmetric horizontal spread.

cards.heading: Edera nigra
cards.notes: Uncapped small clusters and angled to cordate leaves; a faint basal junction is visible on the full scan; a single winding support/axis does not meet the specified doubled crossing.

evidence.mask_spec: Coordinates are XYXY in pixels at reference dimensions. Cover rectangles in warm grey RGB (228,225,215), leaving the rest unchanged. Crop rectangles, juxtapose adjacent halves where applicable, then keep within 800 x 720 pixels. Seed 3506823 sets the order for the recorded preparation. At decision points where the crop concealed a contour, compare the full scan after the masked pass.
evidence.method: One observer fixed the checklist after seeing Yale f35v and the published BnF ivy comparator but before opening the other images. The same observer located and masked headings and then scored shuffled codes. Familiar shapes and preparation exposed specimen identities in some cases. The experiment is caption-masked with incomplete observer blinding. Residual prose beside contours can remain. Counts record depiction only. Separate cuttings and their crossings were never pooled into a single plant. The BnF vine occupies a two-page card with the center gutter. The abbreviated Sloane grape plate adds a second depiction from the same witness. The f60v eleborum illustration, Egerton f46r Herba vitis illustration of a distinct herb, and Sloane f102v plate without the designated Bryonia heading were not treated as substitutes for the named entries.
evidence.rubric:
# Public f35v motif comparison, fixed before opening the additional plates

Previously seen: Beinecke f35v, the black-ivy detail and Ethel Voynich oak-grape note reproduced on p. 24 of Zandbergen's 2012 slides, and full BnF latin 6823 f60r. Expected familiarity with ordinary silhouettes of the named plants. New comparator categories fixed using headings and documented plant names only. Use two compact Tractatus de herbis witnesses as available, Latin 6823 and Egerton 747, preferentially both witnesses per group. Seek the named black ivy and oak/gall tree, with three depicted alternatives (grape, elder and a lobed-leaf rooted herb, white bryony where catalogued). Where the requested entry has multiple drawings, retain all candidates or use separately illustrated entries if the source distinguishes them before viewing, rather than pick a nearest shape. Keep captions and neighboring plants outside the illustration where possible. When contours touch words, neutral mask the text without removing contours and log the exception. Record plates under shuffled codes before joining the identities. This is caption-masked, with one observer and incomplete blinding.

Use only outlines of the drawing: color may locate a contour, but it earns no points. For each feature use 1 visible, 0 visibly discordant or visibly missing on a complete plate, ? genuinely ambiguous or cropped. Record all 12 codes and matched count per region, with possible upper counts for unknowns. Equal weights; no hypothesis test. Describe where matches arise. Multiple manuscripts can transmit a drawing tradition, so report each witness without treating them as independent statistical draws.

Fruit (F)
F1. At least two discrete clusters of three or more rounded enclosed units, counting each unit once; scattered solitary fruits do not count.
F2. At least one such cluster terminates a distinct stalk, with recognizable grouping and no enclosing common fruit body or backing leaf.
F3. No acorn-like cup, enclosing husk, or lobed capsule around the rounded units; mark unknown if outlines are unreadable, zero if no rounded units.

Leaf (L)
L1. At least two individually outlined side leaves attach at distinct levels below the top foliage.
L2. Those side leaves are simple and visibly lobed, with at least two broad rounded lobes per side.
L3. The strongest lobing repeats along the long axis on both sides of the leaf; do not count a three- to five-point palmate leaf, a smooth small leaf, or individual leaflets along a rachis.

Crown/stems (C)
C1. A compact upper foliage outline distinguishable from lower lateral leaves or fruit.
C2. Multiple upward stalks fan toward that upper outline from a relatively narrow common point or band.
C3. Two lower lateral stems visibly cross in front of or around a distinct upright axis; a single fork without crossing does not count.

Roots (R)
R1. Clearly drawn roots and aerial stems meet at a common basal junction.
R2. Major lateral roots or primary branches bear at least three recognizable hooked or curved tips in aggregate.
R3. Strongly asymmetric lateral spread, roughly 2:1 or greater from the stem center measured against opposite side, with the longest root roughly horizontal for much of its run.

For a caption-free target, all 12 features are the prespecified matches; F2 and C3 will also be reported under a sensitivity analysis dropping either if attachment or topology proves uncertain on the scan. The rubric is target-conditioned, so results test specificity among documented controls, not identification in the abstract.
evidence.scoring_key: Per card and region, 1 is visible correspondence, 0 is absent or discordant, ? is obscured or ambiguous. Range counts definite to possible matches.
evidence.sensitivity: Dropping F2 changes fruit-perfect controls from 7 of 12 with 3/3 to the same 7 with 2/2. Dropping C3 preserves all control ranks because C3 is zero for every control. Dropping either criterion leaves the region split unchanged. Ignoring the side-leaf position requirement would raise the foliage match for Latin 6823 galla and glandes because the rounded lobes are visible elsewhere in their drawings.

detail.statement: fleet-fable's corrections settle the generator front for now: a chain with one glyph table and no drift, with whole-word reuse from a memory of 300 words, meets all 17 established facts as a whole book (P-G-007), and one table and one memory per dialect reaches the A/B dialect contrast (P-G-009), the last long-range target we had. Together with this session's notes (sound collapse, slot grammars, re-spaced languages and constructed languages each miss where a learned chain succeeds), the record now says the manuscript's measured regularities are what a scribe copying and varying from a few tables would produce, and none of them shows meaning. Two code changes for the attack layout are in review with different trade-offs: fleet-fable's lays a whole book onto every manuscript page (keeps page order, but a writer can tune text to each position), fleet-opus's draws book pages at random (nothing can be tuned to a page, but the book's order is not the manuscript's); a reviewer should pick one, not both. Next, in order: anchors, where a word can be tied to something outside the text (a label beside a drawn object, with exposure-screened annotators, P-L4-006); the invented-language test only if it predicts something a copying procedure does not; and an end to registering text-statistic facts unless the author first shows that a one-table reuse chain misses them.

detail.statement: The catalogue accurately describes the scope and limits of Ardıç’s 2025 Turkish article. The comparison itself is exhibit-based, with selected examples on pp. 87–90, and p. 90 n. 22 points to a companion interpretation for a complete sentence. P. 80 n. 14 points to a separate, explicitly unfinished ATA table. Its methodological notes 5–8 retain alternatives, permit an exception to consistent one-to-one assignment for harmony, acknowledge omitted characters, and say that old and revised values can appear together. Row 10 also relies on an illustrated bridge traversal order. The separate f33v proceedings article, version pp. 15–16, proposes distinct endings for the first line and displays slash-separated alternatives at five of the seven positions of the first-line transliteration. Taking those alternatives literally gives 108 combinations before applying contextual constraints. These examples document the discretion a fixed, independently reproducible projection would need to resolve.

detail.statement: Second, separate annotator for fleet-sol's P-L4-006 panels, as its check asks. Exposure logged before viewing: I knew Tucker and Talbert's taxa for f5v, f6v, f9r, f24r, f25r, f32r (pilot), f13r, f23v, f30v, f45r (my P-L4-005 round), and I saw the candidates for f36v and f23r when reading the step, so I annotated only f42v and f56r, extracting their folio and canvas ids by script without the names, and had no prior knowledge of a proposal for either. I wrote features and a guess for each on the Yale scans (canvases 1006157 and 1006184) before printing the candidates. f42v: a whorl of about eight broad untoothed lanceolate leaves at mid-stem, a single bare stem ending in one pale yellow star-shaped flower with a dark eye-like centre and spiky rays, sparse brown fibrous roots; guess an Ornithogalum-like Asparagaceae or Gentiana lutea. f56r: one pale stem; two lower branches ending in dark blue rounded bodies fringed by green spiny bracts; above, two blue funnel-shaped flowers and a large coiled branch with paired dark-blue lanceolate leaflets; a braided base; guess Convolvulaceae for the funnel flowers, with the spiny heads suggesting Asteraceae (Cynareae). Reveal: f42v, Tucker and Talbert propose Calathea (Goeppertia) loeseneri, Marantaceae; fleet-sol's masked guess was Paris, Melanthiaceae; mine disagrees with both. f56r, they propose Phacelia campanularia, Boraginaceae in the broad sense; fleet-sol's masked guess Heliotropium agrees with that family; mine (Convolvulaceae) does not, though I recorded the coiled branch that carries the Boraginaceae reading. Features agree better than names: both annotators recorded the star-like terminal structure with a dark centre on f42v and the coiled branch with dark bodies and two dark corollas on f56r. Summary across the masked rounds so far (pilot, P-L4-005, P-L4-006): independent genus or family agreement with the proposed taxa is rare outside the two most published folios, and two annotators rarely agree with each other at family level, so these drawings do not carry enough diagnostic detail to support an anchor at genus level, New World or Old. No anchor follows.

evidence.generators: Pinned vs.generators.g_self_citation and g_grille use the public fit pages. Six additional one-table whole-word-reuse backgrounds use the stationary copy condition of P-R-009/P-J-005 fitted on the public fit pages, with no edit reuse or time drift. The stationary iid and piecewise iid controls have 1,536 possible abstract tokens and Zipf weights proportional to rank^-0.9. In the piecewise case six independent probability vectors each blend 70% randomly permuted Zipf weights and 30% original weights and are assigned to six consecutive equal-page-count groups by floor(6i/P) for zero-based page i. The iid token drawings are independent conditional on the probability vector, so they contain no local transition rule. Generator seeds 901–908, stationary-copy seeds 901–906, iid seeds 901–924.
evidence.input: The public practice Zandbergen–Landini and independent Takahashi transcriptions were intersected on 615 paragraph-line IDs with all tokens certain and in the fixed ordinary EVA letters acdefghiklmnopqrsty. The sample occupies 31 public practice pages. The page and line order of the retained primary lines was kept. Natural controls are contiguous windows with the same token count, sampled using Random(901) from the named pinned works and cut to identical line lengths. These are length-matched illustrations, without a genre or writing-system match. The article’s full manuscript and original corpora are distinct from this layout.
evidence.limitations: Topology measures beyond the explicit degree and selectivity implementations, the approach to language ranking, and the paper’s compatibility density estimates were outside scope. Single windows from four books do not reproduce its language reference distribution. Generated texts illustrate multiple mechanisms behind a rejection. A match to a direction or a null rejection can occur with materially different effect sizes.
evidence.method: Primary ratios use observed metric divided by the permutation mean. The longer manuscript run uses 999 permutations at each of the global, page and line levels, independently in both editions, fixed NumPy seed 98900 plus 100 per successive null. Each two-sided P is twice the smaller add-one tail probability clipped at one, counting ties in each tail. Holm adjusted values cover seven metrics within each edition and each null. The adjacency sensitivity excludes between-line edges on every permutation. I and I50 in that check are unchanged because time still runs across the retained token sequence. Simulations and natural controls use 99 permutations, with unadjusted rejection counts provided only as calibration summaries. All input distinctions are fixed across permutations.

metric_details.B_pairs: Alternate literal reading of duplicated bigrams, the number of ordered adjacent pairs occurring at least twice regardless of whether the two tokens are the same type.
metric_details.B_types: Distinct types with at least one self-adjacency, the literal definition in the first-order Statistics section on p. 7. Table 1 labels B Betweenness and the compatibility prose says duplicated bigrams.
metric_details.I: Mean over word types of frequency at least 5 of population SD of the circular recurrence gaps divided by their mean. Eq. 6 closes the boundary gap so each type’s gaps sum to the stream duration.
metric_details.I50: As for I over the top 50 by count, lexically breaking frequency ties.
metric_details.k_out: Mean distinct outgoing neighbors on the directed adjacency graph described in Methods, retaining a self-loop when present. With fixed length and vocabulary, k_out is directly related to total repeated-edge surplus.
metric_details.s: Mean of twice word count divided by the number of distinct neighbors in either direction, as in Methods. For the seam-exclusion check the convention is to use a denominator of one for a type isolated by removing line boundaries.
metric_details.s50: s over the 50 most frequent types.

evidence.publication_scope: Table 3 reports observed/shuffled mean ratios 1.433 (I), 1.890 (I*), 2.637 (B), and 0.949 (k). Its C* interval 0.981–1.017 is the only displayed one that includes 1. The prose on p. 5 says the other intervals include it, whereas Table 3 and the argument require exclude. The authors report B and I* as exceptions to the comparisons with their natural-language distribution in Table 4. They explicitly propose topic shifts as one reason for increased I*. The authors used ten global shuffles and Eq. 8 error bands. This audit uses permutation tails. Hence its P values cannot be compared numerically to their standardized distances. The article makes no deterministic glyph or language assignment that can be entered as a key.

detail.statement: Amancio et al.’s reported excess intermittency against global token shuffles is reproduced qualitatively in two public practice editions. All 24 independent page-conditional token streams per layout also exceed that null for both intermittency summaries. Preserving each page’s vocabulary and frequencies reduces the Voynich ratios to 1.005–1.016 and removes significance in both editions. attack.json.method: The codebook enumerates the fixed WORD_MAP plus every possible output of decode_token at commit ba3ffea6d517721b389e22af3a67f78db3674e73. Direct entries take precedence, followed by the published no-qo variant and then the k, p, op and t prefix expansions. Entries were expanded from the published finite stem inventory alone. Unknown tokens emit no Italian, matching the reader’s unknown marker. The claim runner uses Zandbergen–Landini EVA, while the author’s reader uses Takahashi EVA. This audit covers the published token resolver and the proposed Italian target. The compiled table agreed with the published function on all 969 generated parity probes, including unknown tokens and prefix collisions. An additional public practice evaluation on Takahashi returned the same five failing checks as Zandbergen–Landini.

step.json.check: To repeat the audit, implement the circular recurrence interval exactly and count adjacent identical types and repeated ordered pairs separately. Predeclare the transliteration, line inclusion, seam handling, metrics, and structured controls, then test whole-token, within-page and within-line permutations. Evaluate the metrics jointly against independent realizations and natural texts before making any claim about the source of the local order signal.

evidence.generators: Pinned vs.generators.g_self_citation and g_grille use the public fit pages. Six additional one-table whole-word-reuse backgrounds use the stationary copy condition of P-R-009/P-J-005 fitted on the public fit pages, with no edit reuse or time drift. The stationary iid and piecewise iid controls have 1,536 possible abstract tokens and Zipf weights proportional to rank^-0.9. In the piecewise case six independent probability vectors each blend 70% randomly permuted Zipf weights and 30% original weights and are assigned to six consecutive equal-page-count groups by floor(6i/P) for zero-based page i. The iid token drawings are independent conditional on the probability vector, so they contain no local transition rule. Generator seeds 901–908, stationary-copy seeds 901–906, iid seeds 901–924.
evidence.input: The public practice Zandbergen–Landini and independent Takahashi transcriptions were intersected on 615 paragraph-line IDs with all tokens certain and in the fixed ordinary EVA letters acdefghiklmnopqrsty. The sample occupies 31 public practice pages. The page and line order of the retained primary lines was kept. Natural controls are contiguous windows with the same token count, sampled using Random(901) from the named pinned works and cut to identical line lengths. These are length-matched illustrations, without a genre or writing-system match. The article’s full manuscript and original corpora are distinct from this layout.
evidence.limitations: Topology measures beyond the explicit degree and selectivity implementations, the approach to language ranking, and the paper’s compatibility density estimates were outside scope. Single windows from four books do not reproduce its language reference distribution. Generated texts illustrate multiple mechanisms behind a rejection. A match to a direction or a null rejection can occur with materially different effect sizes.
evidence.method: Primary ratios use observed metric divided by the permutation mean. The longer manuscript run uses 999 permutations at each of the global, page and line levels, independently in both editions, fixed NumPy seed 98900 plus 100 per successive null. Each two-sided P is twice the smaller add-one tail probability clipped at one, counting ties in each tail. Holm adjusted values cover seven metrics within each edition and each null. The adjacency sensitivity excludes between-line edges on every permutation. I and I50 in that check are unchanged because time still runs across the retained token sequence. Simulations and natural controls use 99 permutations, with unadjusted rejection counts provided only as calibration summaries. All input distinctions are fixed across permutations.

metric_details.B_pairs: Alternate literal reading of duplicated bigrams, the number of ordered adjacent pairs occurring at least twice regardless of whether the two tokens are the same type.
metric_details.B_types: Distinct types with at least one self-adjacency, the literal definition in the first-order Statistics section on p. 7. Table 1 labels B Betweenness and the compatibility prose says duplicated bigrams.
metric_details.I: Mean over word types of frequency at least 5 of population SD of the circular recurrence gaps divided by their mean. Eq. 6 closes the boundary gap so each type’s gaps sum to the stream duration.
metric_details.I50: As for I over the top 50 by count, lexically breaking frequency ties.
metric_details.k_out: Mean distinct outgoing neighbors on the directed adjacency graph described in Methods, retaining a self-loop when present. With fixed length and vocabulary, k_out is directly related to total repeated-edge surplus.
metric_details.s: Mean of twice word count divided by the number of distinct neighbors in either direction, as in Methods. For the seam-exclusion check the convention is to use a denominator of one for a type isolated by removing line boundaries.
metric_details.s50: s over the 50 most frequent types.

evidence.publication_scope: Table 3 reports observed/shuffled mean ratios 1.433 (I), 1.890 (I*), 2.637 (B), and 0.949 (k). Its C* interval 0.981–1.017 is the only displayed one that includes 1. The prose on p. 5 says the other intervals include it, whereas Table 3 and the argument require exclude. established: Stolfi sees a comparatively flat head, small rays, visible bract-like details and diagonal stalks as possible similarities. He reports that only one of the three heads has the flat form and that the large central disk is a weaker match for wild sunflowers.

He describes the manuscript leaves as radially divided, with rounded tips and an apparently central petiole attachment. His sunflower comparators have a heart- or spade-shaped undivided blade and an edge attachment. He reports a further difference in the disk texture and grounds his rejection chiefly on the leaf morphology.

Jerusalem artichoke gives an analogy for the enlarged underground structures, with differences in shape, proportion and leaf attachment. Stolfi leaves wider Asteraceae affinity open and observes that the family is not geographically diagnostic.

open.check: Compare the Yale f33v scan with dated premodern depictions under separate region codes and masks, including an early securely labeled sunflower such as Dodoens 1568 p. 295 and several premodern Old World images with disk-like heads or apparently central leaf attachment. Treat f93r as a separately proposed sunflower in the O’Neill and Tucker–Talbert tradition and never pool the two folios. Score the whole-plant and head-only matches, record missing regions and prior exposures, and require independent scoring before proposing any label anchor.

evidence.alignment: For each homologous pair, take the highest exact score and the highest fuzzy score over all rotations of the second ring in each direction. The ordinal view compares the first min(n,m) positions. The primary equal-arc view compares the midpoints of min(n,m) equal fractions of a ring by projecting each midpoint to both respective slot counts using floor, then advances the second ring through all of its rotations. The method uses ordinal ranks as geometry proxies and makes no claim of exact angular equality. Sensitivity comparisons apply literal clock sorting of the locally anomalous Libra block, or include all full rings on different panels.
evidence.inputs: The pinned ZL3b-n.txt, IT2a-n.txt and RF1b-e.txt contain the same 12 Zodiac panels. P-L4-007 flattens label words per panel, producing 350 ZL words, 367 Takahashi words and 343 RF words. The same set of physical Lz identifiers is used when moving to a locus-level test. Alternatives are parsed according to vs.ivtff and uncertain spaces split.
evidence.interpretation: The exploratory IT flattened exact result varies across editions and loses significance when the comparison uses physical rings and whole labels. Label meanings remain open. The assay can miss a roster if ring segmentation varies by sign, if corresponding slots are displaced by unequal gaps, or if the same category uses divergent word forms.
evidence.legacy_method: For each pair i<j in the supplied order, score the prefix overlap at equal ordinal positions. To optimize alignment, cyclically rotate j by each offset, then truncate the two sequences to the shorter length and sum exact or at-most-one raw EVA character edit matches. Use the best per pair and sum across the 66 pairs. The sensitivity also permits rotating i individually. The original reports 41 and 115; our explicit convention gives 40 and 110. Allowing either side gives 40 and 117. The sample and the unchanged 0.1787% original exact-match fraction are reproducible; the exact optimum depends on unequal-length conventions and the edit unit.
evidence.null_and_power: Use NumPy RNG seed 61304 and 999 permutations. Shuffle labels independently within the applicable page or ring, with missing ring slots fixed. P is the upper-tail add-one rank with ties. For power, use 24 seeds 2401–2424 and 199 shuffles per simulated instance. For each full-ring group independently choose k positions in its shortest ring and project to each ring by the same fractional construction. Rotate each ring’s planted positions independently, keep the original unknowns, then substitute one distinct shared pseudolabel per position where available. Test exact agreement for the same main comparison. Sign-dependent renamings, variable mappings between ring layers and hypotheses with just one stable position are outside this power result.

evidence.ring_method: Interpret each ZL @Lz group as one block of labels following the scan and ZL ring headers. Keep the innermost and outermost full figure rings as separate comparison groups. Cancer has a middle full ring with no primary homologous partner. Exclude four groups from primary comparisons: the Pisces central star and the Gemini, Scorpius and Sagittarius partial rows. One full-locus label joins all its words with an explicit separator. The first-word view retains just its first token. Both are segmented with EVA-basic and label loci containing uncertain or absent tokens retain their geometric slot as a missing observation. Missing observations never match, including another missing observation. Fuzzy similarity is at most one insertion, deletion or substitution of an EVA-basic unit.

scan_checks.observation: The outer-band oees glyph group is immediately clockwise from the crowned figure’s longer label and before the next longer label. This supports the edition order around .8–.10 over a literal 01:45 tag for .8. Literal time sorting is included as a sensitivity.
Cancer has three full bands. The approximate 07:00 comments coincide for distinct adjacent outer loci .11 and .12. The primary data keep their edition order and do not merge them.
Four figures above the outer ring form a separate partial group; the full rings remain distinct.
Four figures sit in a short outer group. The two larger circles can be separately aligned.

detail.statement: The pooled ZL page test reproduces 0.18% exact same-position agreement and gives 40 exact and 110 one-edit agreements after optimizing rotation across 66 pairs. Its 999-permutation P values are 0.246 and 0.312. Takahashi’s flattened exact-word result is nominally unusual at P=0.016 but moves to P=0.081 when the shorter and longer page can each be rotated. The historical layouts contain distinct rings and some partial rows. Using 285 figure-label loci and comparing equal ring positions under independent rotations and both relative directions, the exact whole-label P values are 0.887, 0.846 and 0.899 across the three editions. Planting two repeated positions in both full-ring groups gives detections in 24 of 24 simulations, while one repeated position gives 0 of 24. The result weighs against a broadly shared ordered roster that uses the same visible labels at comparable positions across the rings.

evidence.plan:
# P-L4-002 geometry and ordered-feature check

Past exposure: f69v and the two Bodleian lunar mansion pages, and chapter II opening of the Greater Bundahišn while cataloguing Herrmann. This pass scores by fixed criteria with source-aware preparation and one observer. Three manuscript editions are frozen before retrieving the comparator name lists. Preserve one radial locus per green-ended bar in clockwise ZL locus order. Compare candidate lists in official source order, with all 28 rotations and both directions. No fit of source-specific glyph values. All 28 supports known from previous exposure. The prior has no public mapping for the 20 reported correspondences.

Order-sensitive measures fixed before source extraction. First-symbol equality pattern is a binary partition of the 378 unordered pairs of index positions. Score the Pearson correlation of the manuscript and comparator partitions, maximizing over the identical 56 alignments. A constant vector is uninformative. Use both Arabic orthographic names with articles and bare names stripping only an explicitly specified Arabic definite article (or Latin spellings that directly render it when the edition makes this possible). Report alternative treatment as sensitivity. Phrase lengths count retained glyphs across the locus. Compare normalized average ranks to the comparator's normalized grapheme counts, taking the positive Pearson correlation maximum over the same alignments. Word boundaries, diacritics and source-specific digraphs are conventions to record. Test both scores independently against 3,999 whole-name shuffles of the comparator, holding names with their grapheme counts and initials intact. Treat the families of views as exploratory. Include fixed random-prefix controls and an exact circular rotation positive check. Match the source-label count, per-letter class sizes and lengths through name permutations, with no weight for the shared count of 28.

Visual checks fixed before retrieving additional plate images. Record one visible legend or text group per sector, regularly alternating radial styles, radial separators making enclosed compartments, isolated star groups with variable dot counts, identifiable grouping marks at a different level and a fixed start cue. List unknown where any region is missing or not shown in a documentary text witness. Caption masks are meaningful for images that can be paired to the same criteria. The already recognized Voynich and Bodleian pages provide no independent blinded evaluation of provenance.

Scope: these are structural comparisons applicable only to hypotheses that preserve some first-symbol grouping or length order. No text interpretation and no anchor unless a separately frozen per-slot prediction gains external corroboration.
evidence.scope: This is one-source-aware-observer work with no independent blind annotator. The historical signals are conditional on simple length or first-class preservation. The six spellings or lists and two scores per edition were exploratory, and the three transcriptions represent the same manuscript. The Henry Bate prose and quarter tests followed the initial finding. A result at the table-selected fixed shift does not substitute for an independent fixation of the shift.
evidence.score_details: Compute the Pearson correlation between the 378-element binary equality vectors for initial-class membership, and separately between the average-rank length vectors. A missing RF locus excludes the relevant point and all its initial-class pairs. Candidate length ranks are computed on the complete witness before applying the RF mask. For each score maximize over 56 alignments. Forward index k maps manuscript position i to source (i+k) modulo 28. Reverse index k maps i to 27-((i+k) modulo 28). Thus reverse index 5 maps f69v.4 to the table’s 23rd entry. NumPy random seed 69128 and 3,999 whole-name permutations hold the letter class and length of each candidate entry together. Ties count in the upper tail and the reported P adds one to its numerator and denominator.

source_tables.normalization: Use the ordered printed names as transcribed into the English translation. Count Roman letters and strip spaces or hyphens. This is a spelling witness, with no claim that the editor reproduces medieval Pahlavi letter counts.

source_tables.locus: Al-Farghānī, Golius 1669 edition, printed Arabic pp. 77–79 (LOC scan pages 49–50)
source_tables.normalization: Use head terms and their immediate lexical modifiers, omitting glosses and alternative names. Keep unpointed Arabic letters, treating hamza-bearing letters as one each. Sensitivity removes a leading written definite article from the first word only.

source_tables.normalization: The reported Arabic nomenclature appears in a Persian astronomical work. Use the translation’s romanized terms as printed. Strip combining marks, preserve ʿ and ʾ, count sh, gh, dh, th and kh as single graphemes, and count the written connector in phrases.

source_tables.normalization: Use only the first edited name on each of 28 numbered lines, without editorial apparatus or Latin glosses. Count letters and keep letters restored by the editors. evidence.plan:
# P-L4-002 geometry and ordered-feature check

Past exposure: f69v and the two Bodleian lunar mansion pages, and chapter II opening of the Greater Bundahišn while cataloguing Herrmann. This pass scores by fixed criteria with source-aware preparation and one observer. Three manuscript editions are frozen before retrieving the comparator name lists. Preserve one radial locus per green-ended bar in clockwise ZL locus order. Compare candidate lists in official source order, with all 28 rotations and both directions. No fit of source-specific glyph values. All 28 supports known from previous exposure. The prior has no public mapping for the 20 reported correspondences.

Order-sensitive measures fixed before source extraction. First-symbol equality pattern is a binary partition of the 378 unordered pairs of index positions. Score the Pearson correlation of the manuscript and comparator partitions, maximizing over the identical 56 alignments. A constant vector is uninformative. Use both Arabic orthographic names with articles and bare names stripping only an explicitly specified Arabic definite article (or Latin spellings that directly render it when the edition makes this possible). Report alternative treatment as sensitivity. Phrase lengths count retained glyphs across the locus. Compare normalized average ranks to the comparator's normalized grapheme counts, taking the positive Pearson correlation maximum over the same alignments. Word boundaries, diacritics and source-specific digraphs are conventions to record. Test both scores independently against 3,999 whole-name shuffles of the comparator, holding names with their grapheme counts and initials intact. Treat the families of views as exploratory. Include fixed random-prefix controls and an exact circular rotation positive check. Match the source-label count, per-letter class sizes and lengths through name permutations, with no weight for the shared count of 28.

Visual checks fixed before retrieving additional plate images. Record one visible legend or text group per sector, regularly alternating radial styles, radial separators making enclosed compartments, isolated star groups with variable dot counts, identifiable grouping marks at a different level and a fixed start cue. List unknown where any region is missing or not shown in a documentary text witness. Caption masks are meaningful for images that can be paired to the same criteria. The already recognized Voynich and Bodleian pages provide no independent blinded evaluation of provenance.

Scope: these are structural comparisons applicable only to hypotheses that preserve some first-symbol grouping or length order. No text interpretation and no anchor unless a separately frozen per-slot prediction gains external corroboration.
evidence.scope: This is one-source-aware-observer work with no independent blind annotator. The historical signals are conditional on simple length or first-class preservation. The six spellings or lists and two scores per edition were exploratory, and the three transcriptions represent the same manuscript. The Henry Bate prose and quarter tests followed the initial finding. A result at the table-selected fixed shift does not substitute for an independent fixation of the shift.
evidence.score_details: Compute the Pearson correlation between the 378-element binary equality vectors for initial-class membership, and separately between the average-rank length vectors. A missing RF locus excludes the relevant point and all its initial-class pairs. Candidate length ranks are computed on the complete witness before applying the RF mask. For each score maximize over 56 alignments. Forward index k maps manuscript position i to source (i+k) modulo 28. Reverse index k maps i to 27-((i+k) modulo 28). Thus reverse index 5 maps f69v.4 to the table’s 23rd entry. NumPy random seed 69128 and 3,999 whole-name permutations hold the letter class and length of each candidate entry together. Ties count in the upper tail and the reported P adds one to its numerator and denominator.

detail.check: Lay any whole-book text with the practice draw of code-P-G-007-fleet-opus and count lines that land on more than one evaluation page; it should be zero after the fix.
detail.statement: Two code changes in review give attacks a whole-book layout under the same name (cut book): mine (branch code-R-book-cut-fleet-fable: the text is laid onto every page of the manuscript in order and measured on the evaluation pages) and fleet-opus's (branch code-P-G-007-fleet-opus: the attacker sends a book of at least 226 pages, the scorer draws one book page per evaluation page, in book order, and each evaluation page reads on from its drawn page). P-LEAD-013 asks a reviewer to pick one. I ran the same three one-table texts of the P-G-007 correction through both on the practice split, to see whether the choice changes a verdict. It does. In my layout all 17 established facts hold on 3 of 3 seeds; in the random-draw layout (book cut into pages of 19 lines, the largest that keeps 226 pages inside the 512 KiB limit for a text of this size; paragraph-opening lines spread evenly) F-014, the share of word types occurring once, fails on 2 of 3 seeds and the rest hold. Cause, checked by counting: an evaluation page longer than the attacker's book page reads on into the following book pages, and when the next evaluation page drew one of those, both receive the same lines. On the practice draw two of the 34 evaluation pages run into the next drawn page, and about 50 of the 821 lines laid (6%) are laid twice (21 lines, 2.6%, with pages of 23 lines; my count takes every line from the ordinary stream, so it is approximate). Repeated stretches lower the singleton share, which is what F-014 measures, and they must also raise page-to-page similarity and reuse for the pages involved, which favours an attacker on F-009, F-011 and F-016; so the defect cuts both ways and is not a matter of taste between the two designs. An attacker cannot avoid it: book pages long enough for the longest manuscript pages would put a 226-page book far over the size limit. Fix within that design: draw the pages as now, but let each evaluation page read from where the previous one stopped if that is later than its own drawn page (never the same line twice). What I have not checked: the held-out draw (it comes from the season seed), other page sizes, and whether F-014 still fails once lines are not repeated. On the difference that is a matter of judgement, as P-LEAD-013 puts it: in my layout a procedure can fit its text to a position in the book (the drifting window and the per-dialect tables do exactly that); in the random-draw layout it cannot, and position still roughly follows book order. Either is defensible; the one-table text needs neither. Nothing here is scored on hidden pages.

model.json.statement: Components were chosen by greedy forward selection under 4-fold cross-validation over scribe 1's public training pages only (pool: vocab, chain, position, letters order 2-5, copy windows 3/5/10/20/50 with 0 or 1 edits, templates prefix 0-3 x suffix 0-3), stopping when a component gained under 0.002 bits per word. Cross-validated: 11.31 bits per word against 11.75 for the bag of words and 11.40 for glyph trigrams alone. The same search run separately on scribes 2, 3 and 4 and on the whole text picked the same core every time (letters order 3 first; copy with a wide window; position; templates), with cross-validated gains over the bag of 0.39, 0.39, 0.58 and 0.38 bits per word; scribe 5 has too few training words. In every scope most of the gain is glyph trigrams alone, the word-to-word chain is selected late or never (under 0.01 bits per word), and the memorized vocabulary is never selected once letters order 3 is in. Negative side: nothing in the current component language gets much below a glyph trigram model (0.04 to 0.16 bits per word), so a production process is not yet separated from spelling habit.
model.json.title: Scribe 1: glyph trigrams + page-local copy (window 50, exact and one-glyph-changed) + line position + prefix templates + chain
